summary: Both M1 and M2 are correctly resolved. _SERIES_ACRONYM_RE is now derived from _ACRONYM_ALIASES via _acronym_to_pattern() with no hand-typed alternation, the built pattern is a pure re.escape-d literal alternation (one branch scoped case-insensitive for zamac) with no unbounded quantifiers, confirmed ReDoS-safe by direct timing probes (worst case ~4ms on ~50-200KB adversarial input, far under the 100ms bar). Behavioral checks (SDCC/RLC/STH case sensitivity, lowercase zamac match, full 8/8 fixture) all pass, and the full suite is green (1244 passed). deployment.md's new note is accurate and correctly placed in the Staged rollout section. One pre-existing minor doc comment (line ~131) was left stale by the fix and should be tightened in a follow-up.

suggestions.suggestion: The SERIES_LEXICON header comment at line 131 still reads: "Aliases resolve case-insensitively EXCEPT the short/ambiguous acronyms in `_ACRONYM_ALIASES`, which are matched case-sensitively to avoid prose collisions (e.g. prose \"sth\"/\"rlc\")." This is now imprecise: `zamac` is a member of `_ACRONYM_ALIASES` but, per the new `_CASE_INSENSITIVE_ACRONYMS` carve-out, is matched case-INsensitively, not case-sensitively as this sentence implies. The more detailed comment block above `_SERIES_ACRONYM_RE` (lines ~296-312) does correctly document the split, so this is purely a stale summary one screen away, not a functional issue.
suggestions.benefit: Keeps the two self-documenting comment blocks in the same file from contradicting each other, avoiding confusion for the next person who edits the acronym set and only reads the nearer (older) comment.

derivation_covers_all_aliases.verdict: all 4 aliases present in the derived branch list, no silent drop; _ACRONYM_BRANCHES is a list comprehension over the full _ACRONYM_ALIASES frozenset so a future alias addition is automatically covered

redos_safety.structure: pure re.escape-d literal alternation, one branch scoped (?i:...), no \s+/\s*/.*/nested quantifiers
redos_safety.verdict: linear-time, all probes well under 100ms even at 4x the requested ~50KB size -> confirmed ReDoS-safe
